reports.task:
完成以下局部调查问题，查找直接证据并说明适用范围：Where is the iron pillar in the image located?
背景声明：The iron pillar in Qutub Minar has the names of the ancestors of the Mughals proving that they built it.
声明日期（任务元数据）：2023-02-20

findings.statement: The pictured iron pillar is the Loha Stambha at Jawahar Burj in Lohagarh Fort (Bharatpur Fort), Bharatpur, Rajasthan, India. It is not the iron pillar in Delhi’s Qutub Minar complex.
limitations: The location is identified by the retrieved Alt News and NewsMobile reports. The official heritage webpage and linked original photographs were inaccessible, preventing independent verification against those primary sources.

evidence.label: Photo of iron pillar in Bharatpur fort falsely shared to claim Mughals’ ‘Hindu ancestry’ by Sarvesh38453373, Pradip Kr. Singh – Alt News
evidence.content:
[1] The Qutub Minar is a UNESCO world heritage site in South Delhi. The name literally means victory tower. Qutbu’d-Din Aibak laid the foundation of this monument in 1199 AD and it was later completed by his successor and son-in-law Shamsu’d-Din Iltutmish. The Qutub complex in Mehrauli, Delhi, illustrates magnificent ancient and medieval indo-islamic architecture. In this complex lies an iron pillar, known as the Kirti stambh (victory column) which was built by Chandragupta II in (circa) the 3rd or 4th Century CE.
